newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open flat on thin fund activity.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open flat on thin fund activity.

text.p: Singapore shares opened flat on Monday morning with institutional buying and selling very subdued, dealers said.
"I personally think we will end today almost unchanged," said a dealer with a large European securities house.
"Either flat or perhaps a bit firmer on the back of economic data," predicted another.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was down 2.73 points at 2,052.63 by 0150 GMT with 32.2 million shares traded.
Dealers the absence of London traders in the afternoon due to a U.K. public holiday would keep fund activity to a minimum.
But underlying sentiment appeared to be positive following Friday's record high on Wall St and better news on the economy.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 87.78 points to close at 7,345.91 on Friday, a fresh high.
Last week saw the publication of the first positive export figures for Singapore in five months.
Few stocks stood out in early trade with early volume split between a number of blue chips and over-the-counter shares.
Singapore Telecom was up one cent at Singapore $2.48 ahead of its full-year results due out on Friday.
